source.title: On the Relationship Between Double Descent of CNNs and Shape/Texture Bias Under Learning Process
source.authors: Shun Iwase; Shuya Takahashi; Nakamasa Inoue; Rio Yokota; Ryo Nakamura; Hirokatsu Kataoka; Eisaku Maeda

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reuses the epoch-wise double-descent setup attributed to Nakkiran et al. and measures test error across training epochs, then varies several experimental conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error learning curves and explicit statements about epoch-wise double descent. Shape/texture-bias trajectories and their correlations with test error are also reported; these are recorded as related findings not covered by the listed claim versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the Nakkiran et al. epoch-wise setup (ResNet18, CIFAR-10, 20% label noise, Adam lr 1e-4, 1,000 epochs) and plots test error over epochs. It states where double descent appears or is absent across label-noise levels, initializations, datasets and architectures. Its main aim is shape/texture bias, but its own test-error results bear on V2 and on V6's noise dependence. One difference from the original: the baseline uses ImageNet-pretrained weights, while a scratch run appears only as an ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add three points: the bias–error correlation disappears once the second descent begins (Phase 3); synchronization appears only in the final conv layer; and synchronization fails for EfficientNetB0. The authors do not claim that shape/texture features cause double descent; they argue the relation is more complex than that.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Nakkiran et al. epoch-wise double-descent setting as its baseline and measures test error over epochs, while adding shape/texture-bias measurements and several ablations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported bias/test-error synchronization varies by training phase, initialization, dataset, label-noise proportion, and architecture; EfficientNetB0 has a bias spike around epoch 10.

fits_no_version.finding: Shape/texture bias in the final conv layer shows double descent/ascent that correlates with test error in Phases 1–2 but not Phase 3. The correlation varies by dataset and architecture; EfficientNetB0 shows none. Bias DD/ascent appears even at p = 0. Only the 17th layer shows a clear transition (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Before the second descent, CNN shape/texture bias in the last conv layer tracks epoch-wise test error; after it, the relation vanishes.

record.problems: Most learning-curve outcomes are presented in figures without numerical test-error values or uncertainty estimates. The CIFAR-100 phase 1/2 correlations conflict between Table 2 and the prose. The text does not separately state whether test-error double descent occurs for each alternative initialization, dataset, or architecture.

untested.parts: Numeric test-error values, peak height and peak epoch are not reported in text (figures only). Generality beyond small CNNs on CIFAR is untested.
All; no capacity sweep or non-deep model classes.
Variance as driver, multiple/triple descent, and removal under optimally tuned regularization.

missing.what: Phase 3 correlations for MobileNetV2 (−0.016, 0.036, 0.026) and DenseNet121 (0.293, −0.289, 0.291)
Layer-wise bias (layers 5, 9, 13, 17): only layer 17 shows a clear transition
Statement that the second descent does not reach below the first-descent minimum

record.verdict_notes: Test-error DD is shown only in figures, with no numeric error values or uncertainty. The baseline uses ImageNet pretraining, unlike Nakkiran. V2 states for R5–R10 rest on inference from the text and phase tables, so researchers should check the figures. The p = 0 result was given limits_scope rather than challenges for V2, because the authors and V6 treat noise as the condition for the effect.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error measurement across model sizes.
The paper studies epoch-wise behavior in its stated CNN training settings, not whether the curve is universal across networks or training procedures.
No sweep over the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes or general test of post-interpolation risk.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested as a predictor of peak location.

The study varies label-noise proportion and reports its relationship to test-error double descent. It does not test variance as a driver, multiple or triple descent, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number or test of whether that yields an ordinary U-shaped curve.
